transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-08-13 15:00 PDT / 22:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Devon Patel, Ravi Kapoor (Redwood); Elena Morales, Gabe Fisher, Tanya Iqbal, Samir Desai (Orchard Runway)

[00:00] Maya (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. i see we have a full table — elena, gabe, tanya, samir from orchard and devon/ravi from our side. quick intros and then we'll jump to the network and security items first.
[00:23] Elena (Head of MLOps): hi, thanks for doing this. we wanted to make sure the private deployment story is ironed out — our compliance team is pretty strict, so the VPC/on-prem options are key.
[00:37] Gabe (Platform Eng): and from infra we'll need peering details, allowed ports, that kind of thing — plus we want to run a small pilot before committing to reserved capacity.
[00:51] Devon (CSM): perfect, scope sounds clear — pilot, security review, then ops sprint. ravi will cover the staging and perf stuff.
[01:05] Ravi (SE): yep. at a high level, for private we do a customer-managed VPC with a control plane handshake. the usual components: model runtime on our managed nodes, kms integration, audit logs streamed to your splunk or s3, and optional on-prem runtime if you need air-gap.
[01:26] Tanya (Security): quick Q — do you support HSM-backed keys? and how do you handle key rotation for cached tokens?
[01:40] Ravi (SE): we integrate with customer KMS/HSM via a secure connector, keys can be customer-managed. rotation is supported — we push key updates to the runtime and have a rolling cache invalidation. there may be a brief reconnection window but no token leak; i'll share the design doc.
[01:58] Samir (SRE): curious about audit log retention — our policy is 7 years for some events, is that feasible?
[02:11] Maya (AE): we offer configurable retention; long-term cold storage can be routed to your s3 with lifecycle policies. we'll include retention SLAs in the security pack.
[02:25] Elena: great. next, pilot goals — we want to validate latency under our typical prompt mix. target p95 under 400ms and cost roughly within our token budget.
[02:40] Ravi: good to know. can you share a representative prompt set? sequence length distribution, percent embeddings vs generation?
[02:51] Elena: yes, i'll get that today. most calls are short generation (~30-64 tokens) with some longer summarization jobs (~512 tokens) about 10% of the time. embeddings used for search are small and frequent.
[03:07] Gabe: also important — we use Istio in our mesh, and we'd like to terminate TLS at sidecar. will that affect the handshake to the control plane?
[03:20] Ravi: we can support mTLS at the edge; the runtime expects inbound TLS — if you're doing sidecar termination we'll need a small NAT or a passthrough so our connector can validate certs. i'll put together network flows.
[03:37] Maya: i'm noting network owner gabe will share CIDR and a contact.

[05:10] [quick mid-call recap]
Maya: recap so far — security requirements (tanya), networking (gabe), pilot SLOs (elena), staging runbook (ravi). next up: observability and rollout plan.

[05:35] Ravi: on observability, redwood console gives per-route latency and token-level cost breakdowns, traces for request chains, and quality regression alerts tied to eval sets. for the pilot we recommend enabling token-level billing and the perf tracing hook.
[05:56] Elena: can we send traces to our datadog?
[06:07] Ravi: yes — we have exporters for datadog and splunk, and we can also push raw logs to an s3 bucket. note that trace sampling defaults to 10% in pilot but we can bump it.

[06:30] Gabe: on model selection, are you recommending a quantized variant to save cost? our workload is latency-sensitive so i worry about accuracy drop.
[06:45] Ravi: good question. for the short prompts you described, a 4-bit quantized variant typically preserves quality within a fraction of a point on most evals, but for the summarization jobs we may pick a mixed strategy: run long sequences on a higher-precision variant and short queries on quantized. our optimize toolkit can propose a config. we'll run A/B during the pilot.
[07:10] Tanya: compliance question — what about PII redaction and data-in-transit encryption between services?
[07:21] Maya: redwood handles transit encryption by default and offers optional prefix/KV caching rules that can be disabled to avoid storing sensitive prefixes. we also will provide docs for data handling and a standard DPA.

[08:05] Elena: timeline — we'd like pilot running in two weeks and a go/no-go decision after the staging benchmark. is that doable?
[08:16] Ravi: two weeks is tight but OK for a limited pilot if we get prompt set and VPC/CIDR info this week and you provision a staging VPC peering. the benchmark run itself we can schedule for 2026-08-25 as discussed.
[08:31] Gabe: can you outline the staging steps? we want a clear runbook to hand to ops.
[08:40] Ravi: sure — i'll prepare a runbook: 1) network peering + firewall rules, 2) credentials + KMS handshake, 3) deploy model variant to staging pool, 4) run synthetic workload then your real prompt set, 5) collect traces/metrics, 6) joint analysis and tuning. expect a 2-3 hour window for the benchmark.

[09:12] Devon (CSM): from an onboarding cadence pov, we'll do weekly 30-minute standups and a longer 1-hour checkpoint around the benchmark. i'll set the meetings.

[10:00] Elena: procurement and contract — we need to see pricing ranges for pilot vs dedicated. don't need exact numbers now but a ballpark to budget.
[10:12] Maya: i'll send a pilot pricing sheet; for dedicated/reserved we can provide tiers. we'll flag where additional discounts apply for annual commits.

[12:40] [small side conversation about model variants and fallbacks]
Ravi: also want to call out smart routing — if a particular cluster is busy we can fallback to a compatible variant in another region or lower-cost tier to keep service online. that could matter in peak windows.
[13:05] Gabe: fine, but we need to know what that does to latency. fallback to another region might break your 400ms p95.
[13:16] Ravi: agreed, breakpoints will be in the runbook; policy is configurable — can set strict latency SLOs and disable fallback for critical routes.

[15:22] Tanya: security doc specifics — please include SOC2 control mappings, SSO/SAML flow, RBAC model, and encryption at rest details. also we need a contact for pen test coordination.
[15:34] Maya: noted — i'll include SOC2/ISO appendix, SSO schematics, RBAC options, and our security partnerships for pen tests. i'll cc our trust team.

[18:00] Samir: incident ops — how do we handle failover and OOMs, are there graceful degradations?
[18:12] Ravi: runtime supports graceful degradation: lower token limits, route to smaller model variant, or queue requests during spikes. we also have automatic KV/prefix cache invalidation to avoid memory leaks. all of that is in the ops runbook.

[23:40] [customer asks for references and benchmark examples]
Maya: we have a public benchmark doc and a couple of anonymized case studies where customers hit similar goals. i'll share links.

[25:00] Elena: ok i'm comfortable with the plan, the key dependencies are: security pack from redwood, VPC/CIDR from our infra, and the prompt set. once those land we can proceed.

[25:32] Maya: great. recap and owners — maya will send security docs and network diagram; ravi will push runbook and test harness; elena will share prompt set; gabe will provide network details. we'll reconvene after the artifacts are exchanged and schedule the benchmark.

[25:58] Ravi: small note on metrics — please capture p50/p95/p99, token cost per route, and quality regression probes (we'll provide a simple eval harness).

[26:15] Gabe: do you have a standard eval harness or should we feed our own?
[26:21] Ravi: we'll provide a base harness (python scripts + k6 load driver) and you can plug in your prompt set. i'll include instructions for running in your staging project.

[27:00] Tanya: last security item — how's access control for logs? we can't have engineers from other teams see sensitive request payloads.
[27:12] Maya: logs can be role-scoped; we redact request text for non-authorized roles and keep full logs only in customer-owned buckets if you prefer.

[30:00] [logistics conversation: times, contacts, legal handoff]
Maya: legal — i'll route the DPA and pilot terms to your procurement contact after this call. pricing sheet and security pack will be attached.

[31:05] Elena: procurement will want a basic SOW — can you do a one-page SOW for the pilot?
[31:12] Maya: yes, i'll do a one-page SOW outlining scope, pilot duration (3 weeks), acceptance criteria, and next steps.

[33:40] [closing technical clarifications]
Ravi: couple of gotchas — if you have heavy long-sequence jobs, make sure your staging pool has enough memory for attention caches; quantized variants need CPU/GPU kernels that we select at compile time, so we'll recommend hardware profiles in the runbook.

[35:00] Elena: noted. for the pilot we have one g4-like pool in staging, can we get an opinion on whether that's sufficient?
[35:12] Ravi: we'll look at your prompt lengths and throughput target; likely need at least a mid-tier A100 or equivalent for long summaries, but the short generation jobs run fine on Ampere T4-ish. i'll put hardware recs in the runbook.

[40:00] [random crosstalk and minor transcription errors]
Speaker 7: (inaudible)

[43:00] Maya: okay team, final recap — owners and due dates in action items. devon will set the cadence (weekly 30m). we will plan the benchmark week of 2026-08-25.
[43:20] Devon: i'll send calendar invites after the security docs are shared.

[44:00] Elena: thanks all, excited to get started.
[44:10] Gabe: yep, thanks, we'll send the CIDR and contact by tomorrow EOD.
[44:20] Tanya: thanks, we'll prepare compliance questions based on the docs.
[44:30] Maya: talk to you all soon, bye.

End of transcript. Some sections of audio were low volume and speaker attribution may be off in a few places.
